items.summary: Meta Reality Labs ported the AOSP Cuttlefish virtual-device framework to run natively on macOS with Apple silicon, consolidating its dual Goldfish and Cuttlefish emulator platforms. The team revived QEMU support after it had fallen out of use, relaxing Linux-only build gates so vhost-user frontends and libraries could compile on Mac. They increased the HVF tracking-slot count in QEMU's Hypervisor.framework backend to accommodate larger configurations, adopted a native Cocoa display with BGRA pixel-format and mouse-click-as-touch features instead of relying on WebRTC, and added Darwin build support plus JIT entitlements for code signing and notarization. The unified platform cut maintenance burden, reduced infrastructure needs, eliminated redundant tooling, improved fidelity, and lets developers test against the same high-fidelity virtual devices used in CI—now shared with external ecosystem builders as qemu-wearables and cuttlefish-wearables.
items.title: Cuttlefish on Mac: Running Android's Virtual Device Framework Natively on Apple Silicon

items.summary: Human motion offers roboticists a starting point, but robots cannot copy human joint movements directly because their proportions and ranges differ. The open-source NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter adapts human motion to robot-specific anatomy using the shared representation in NVIDIA SOMA-X. It reads Biovision Hierarchy animations on the base skeleton, scales targets, solves inverse kinematics via Newton built with NVIDIA Warp, applies corrections like foot-plant adjustments, and outputs CSV trajectories for downstream learning or control systems. The v0.2 release includes sample motions from BONES-SEED plus reference results for five humanoid robots: Unitree G1, H2, Booster T1, AgiBot X2 Ultra, and A3T3.
items.title: Adapting Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter

items.summary: OpenAI and Databricks have partnered so enterprises can run frontier OpenAI models on business data they already govern in Databricks, while rolling AI use out beyond analysts. Greg Brockman likens using AI without company data to hiring someone with 20 PhDs who is never invited to a meeting. The collaboration centers on three patterns: the Genie plugin lets employees ask questions like product managers do; Unity Gateway gives leaders visibility and cost controls over Codex usage by engineers; and Databricks Apps hosts custom agents built in Agent Bricks or via the OpenAI Agents SDK under Unity Catalog governance. Both companies provide early model access, with GPT-6 family models supported.
items.title: OpenAI and Databricks Partnership Brings Frontier AI to Governed Enterprise Data

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia following reported affairs with an executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The fallout persists, with criticism mounting over apparent inaction by US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick. Lucy Hough spoke with the Guardian's Aisha Down about developments as of publication.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Fallout Continues Amid Criticism of US Commerce Secretary's Inaction

items.summary: A critical Microsoft outage lasting more than 22 hours disrupted services like Outlook, affecting around 430 million users across over 70 countries. The failure stemmed from automated checks that overloaded servers during gradual recovery. Flora Hamilton called it a stark reminder of reliance on digital systems, while Walter Pasquarelli noted governments and businesses now see their vulnerabilities plainly.
items.title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

items.summary: Paul Cristiano, OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director, warned at a Toronto lecture series that an AI accident may kill most people present. He defined an 'AI takeover' as goal-pursuing systems controlling Earth like the US military does today, risking mass death or uninhabitable conditions. Admitting no quantitative model exists to price this risk, he said rapid development could make it a coin flip, with meaningful danger within six to 12 months and high odds even under realistic policy responses.
items.title: OpenAI board member warns AI takeover could be months away

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for failing to oversee high-spec Nvidia chip exports as the Jensen Huang affair widens. Megaspeed was probed over suspected smuggling but remains off the entity list despite agencies favoring its inclusion. Trump had barred chips above H100s; Democrats and ranking members Neal and Wyden are investigating alleged national security risks, with a 25% tariff on H200 imports.
items.title: Pressure mounts on Trump's Commerce Secretary Lutnick amid Nvidia export scandal fallout

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid allegations of an affair with a Chinese government-linked executive, triggering concerns about the world's top chipmaker. His departure may tighten U.S. export controls as China stockpiles restricted chips; in H1, Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators to China (down 44%, 34% of market), while Huawei reached 572,000 units at 28%. Chinese alternatives remain essential but lag.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Exit and Its Impact on China's AI Supply Chain

items.summary: WIRED journalist Steven Levy recounts interviewing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at SIGGRAPH in July 2024, where Nvidia's daughter Madison coordinated questions around slides—suggesting a controlled narrative rather than an open interview. Huang dominated the session, evaded questions about data-center environmental impact, then held an adoring Q&A before meeting Mark Zuckerberg. Levy later interviewed Huang again in December 2024 but concluded that Huang intensely wanted to control his story. Built on immigrant-founder lore—Denny's dinners, Sunday work, a tattooed logo—and the myth of a flat ~35-person organization, this narrative has begun reading as Greek tragedy: Huang's apparent judgment lapses led him to resign from the company he built.
items.title: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale

items.summary: OpenAI launched a wallet feature Friday letting its agents, called dots, help users choose products and complete purchases. It is initially available to limited U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ with eligible Visa, Mastercard or American Express cards. Users review items, totals and card details before checkout, approve via Face ID or fingerprint, and still earn rewards.
items.title: ChatGPT's New Wallet Lets AI Agents Shop and Check Out for You

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang became embroiled in a dual crisis of personal infidelity and alleged national-security ties to China. After admitting he cheated on his wife, reports emerged that he had extramarital relationships with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice president reporting directly to him, plus another unnamed employee. Separately, officials suspect Megaspeed executive Alice Huang—a Chinese citizen—was a spy feeding Beijing information; she was reportedly linked to Huang and connected to Shanghai Century Litong, which facilitated $7.5 billion in chip purchases. Following the affair revelations, Nvidia’s board accepted his resignation on November 13, 2026, naming CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while launching an independent investigation. Huang agreed to testify before Congress amid Democratic and Republican probes into how Trump administration officials handled Nvidia's advanced H200 chip sales to China.
items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder-CEO since 1993, was defenestrated on November 12 and replaced by his CFO as interim leader. Unlike Jobs or Musk, whose flaws were forgiven for their contributions, Huang reportedly couldn't survive romance-scandal reports. Researcher Kristy Loke warns a successor will struggle to replicate his geopolitical deftness—born in Taiwan with White House influence—and Trump's regard, suggesting 'perhaps a Tim Cook' rather than a Jobs.
items.title: Five Skills Jensen Huang's Nvidia Successor Must Master After His Ouster

items.summary: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins released XYBench, a benchmark of 8,115 questions drawn from Stack Overflow (1,557), Stack Exchange (184), manual curation (102), and WikiHow guides (6,272). It tests whether AI assistants recognize the 'XY problem'—when users ask for help with a mistaken approach rather than their true goal—and redirect them accordingly. Five models were evaluated in single-turn settings; all included solutions to the stated request more often than the underlying goal, and focused on it less than humans did. Sonnet 4.5 served as an automated judge, validated by human reviewers at agreement rates from 74.2% to 100%. An oracle experiment showing intent supplied alongside questions only modestly improved results suggests detecting intent is necessary but insufficient; models must also act on divergent goals. The benchmark currently covers English-language procedural queries and remains limited in scope.
items.title: XYBench Benchmarks AI Assistants on Correcting User Misconceptions

items.summary: As leaders gather at the United Nations in Geneva next week to consider a treaty on autonomous weapons, experts warn that machines have already killed soldiers in eastern Ukraine and three civilians in Zaporizhzhia. The first such incident occurred two years ago when AI-identified targets led drones near Bakhmut to kill combatants. Machine-learning systems exhibit emergent behavior, making their choices unpredictable and unexplainable as law requires. Kill decisions are also deeply networked rather than stemming from discrete human judgment. The International Committee of the Red Cross has called for outright prohibition. Existing laws struggle because they rely on individual intent while humans increasingly surrender cognitive functions to machines. A July incident involving a Russian drone that killed three Ukrainians illustrates how targets selected by category, not victims, evade accountability when drones operate in dark mode using commercial chips.
items.title: AI-Driven Autonomous Weapons Demand New Rules as UN Considers Treaty in Geneva

items.summary: Google announced expanded AI agent observability, evaluation, and cost controls spanning its first-party (1P) agents in BigQuery and Looker plus custom third-party (3P) agents built with frameworks like the Agent Development Kit or LangGraph. The rollout centers on a unified telemetry framework that captures logging from every agent into customer-owned BigQuery tables for analysis across familiar tools. Google separates operational metrics such as request volume, latency, and token usage from sensitive conversation content to balance diagnostics with privacy, offering governed logging, fail-closed guardrails around row- or column-level security, in-warehouse root cause analysis via AI functions, and full trace trees for custom agents through the open-source ADK plugin. FinOps controls include per-query byte scan caps using dry-run estimates and daily token quotas to curb runaway spend.
items.title: AI Agent Observability and Governance Across BigQuery and Looker

items.summary: Christoph Trattner argues that news recommender systems should distinguish between attention and intention, so users can correct inferred interests without losing followed sources. He notes Meta's October 13 controls accept feedback in users' own words, Instagram offers topic resets across Feed, Reels and Explore, and TikTok provides keyword filters. A reset relearns from later interactions but does not keep a removed interest out; an explicit correction should instead stay effective for its stated duration unless the user changes it. European law already requires explainable recommenders and non-profiling options, with 2025 minor-protection guidelines recommending permanent resets. Trattner calls for controls that honor their promises over time rather than curing polarization or replacing safe defaults.
items.title: News Recommender Controls and Deliberate Correction

items.summary: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins released XYBench, a benchmark of 8,115 real-world questions that tests whether large language models recognize when users ask based on misconceptions—known as the 'XY problem'—and redirect them toward their actual goal. Drawing from Stack Overflow, Stack Exchange, manual curation, and WikiHow guides, the benchmark evaluates three response aspects: pragmatic solution inclusion, emphasis, and misconception identification. Across five evaluated models—including Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro—every model was more likely to address the literal request than the underlying goal. The work won Best Resource Paper at EMNLP 2026.
items.title: XYBench Benchmarks AI Assistants on Correcting Misguided Questions

items.summary: Shares of Genting Singapore fell more than 6% at 57 cents after the company reported a third quarter of shrinking profits. Net profit dropped 42% to $54.7 million and revenue declined 13% to $566.1 million for the three months ended Sept 30, with both figures also lower than the prior quarter.
items.title: Genting Singapore Shares Fall on Weaker Q3 Profits Amid Resort Revamp

items.summary: Singapore's Lamborghini dealer EuroSports Global reported a net loss widening to $1.24 million in the quarter ended Sept 30, from $752,000 earlier, as revenue fell over 30% to $7.83 million. For its first half, losses rose 57% to $2.29 million with revenue down 21.7% to $15.1 million. The group cites heavy registration fees and cautious buyers; it plans new Urus SE deliveries in the Oct–Dec quarter and a Temerario by March 2027, while seeking funding for its electric motorcycle business.
items.title: EuroSports Global Reports Widening Losses and Seeks Funding Amid Luxury Car Slowdown

items.summary: Logician Jan von Plato led a Helsinki University project to decode 16 of Kurt Gödel's early-1940s notebooks, written partly in obsolete Gabelsberger shorthand. Progress was slow until he enlisted the AI model Claude, which within days produced a comprehensive digest revealing hundreds of previously unknown theorems. Von Plato verified findings through the proof assistant Coq: 663 extracted results yielded about 400 confirmed, roughly 200 repaired and around 50 false statements. The workbooks also contain themes anticipating results from the 1970s-80s that have not been pursued.
items.title: AI Unlocks Hidden Theorems in Kurt Gödel's Posthumous Workbooks

items.summary: Tesla removed its $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from the US configurator. The cheapest orderable dual-motor version is now the Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump over nine months since February launch. Two remaining trims also rose: Premium RWD and Premium AWD each went up $1,000 from their February prices of $44,990 and $48,990. The cheapest AWD Model Y thus climbed 19%, to a level where Chevrolet’s Equinox EV LT 1 AWD ($40,295) and Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD ($40,795) undercut it by more than $9,000. Tesla gave no explanation; plausible reasons include scarce build slots or weak sales of the base trim.
items.title: Tesla kills $41,990 Model Y AWD: all-wheel drive now costs $8,000 more

items.summary: CleanTechnica's Zach and Scott compare Tesla to Apple, arguing the automaker occupies a similar dominant niche position in electric vehicles. Globally, EV share of new sales reached 32% (or 23% counting only BEVs), yet Tesla sells just two models while remaining the second-best-selling BEV producer worldwide, trailing Chinese giant BYD or Geely with plug-in hybrids. In the US, where competition is limited by blocked Chinese imports, Tesla's EV share exceeds 50%, compared to Apple's iPhone holding roughly 20-22% globally and about 58% of the US market.
items.title: Is Tesla The Apple Of The EV Industry?

items.summary: At this week's COP31 climate conference in Turkey, organizers proposed raising electricity's share of global final energy demand to 35% by 2035 from just over 20%, a goal requiring widespread adoption across transportation, industry, and heating. Electrification is framed as essential for cutting fossil fuel dependence, improving efficiency through centralized power generation rather than wasteful localized combustion, and reducing reliance on imported oil amid Middle East conflict-driven price spikes — prompting the EU to target 46% by 2040.
items.title: 'Electrify Everything' Hits the Global Stage at COP31 and Beyond

items.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed International has come under scrutiny over its business connections with China and alleged access to restricted US technology. The company reportedly received funding from Chinese giant Alibaba and purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips, per analyst estimates cited by CNN. These revelations highlight the complex network of international investors, suppliers and data-centre operators in global AI infrastructure.
items.title: Alibaba Funding, Singapore Base, $4 Billion Nvidia Chips: Inside Megaspeed's Global AI Network

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a successor to Jensen Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid revelations of extramarital affairs. Analysts had floated Haas' name; he spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013 and became its CEO in 2022. He is among several candidates with no guarantee. Colette Kress serves as interim CEO.
items.title: Nvidia Approaches Arm CEO Rene Haas as Jensen Huang Successor Candidate

items.summary: On Nov 13, AI-related US stocks fell again as neoclouds led losses amid fresh jitters over AI financing following Jensen Huang's abrupt exit from Nvidia. The Nasdaq-100 dropped 2%, on pace to erase ~$800 billion in value; the Philadelphia Semiconductor index shed 5.1%.
items.title: AI-Related Stocks Slide Again After Nvidia Turmoil

items.summary: Microsoft reported progress but not full recovery after a Thursday outage affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot across more than 70 countries. UK police advised against online crime reporting; schools in Australia and Japan went analog. At least one company delayed an earnings call. Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack as Jensen Huang drew attention away from the incident.
items.title: Microsoft Reports Progress After Global Outage

items.summary: Reed argues Jensen Huang's fatal error was over-involvement in Washington, where technologists' long-horizon thinking clashes with two-year election cycles. His friendship with Trump and Nvidia's presidential backing made his China-exporting worldview seem successful but proved a mirage ending in hearings and investigations. The allegations remain unproven, yet fighting back is the wrong instinct—"In DC, you can't ever really win." This crisis motivates Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World convening next week to burst the bubble.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Biggest Mistake Was Getting Too Involved in DC

items.summary: Nvidia has reportedly begun searching for a permanent chief executive after long-time leader Jensen Huang departed, with three Indian-origin executives emerging as potential candidates. Sanjay Mehrotra, Nikesh Arora and Thomas Kurian are among the names being discussed, according to India Today. The company's board is considering both internal and external options amid what could be a major leadership transition at the US-based chipmaker.
items.title: Who Will Be Nvidia's Next CEO? Three Indian-Origin Tech Leaders in the Spotlight

items.summary: OpenAI is launching a payment wallet built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, available at launch to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the U.S. Each purchase requires identity verification such as Face ID or fingerprint scan, after which users add a card once; transactions charge their selected card while preserving rewards and protections. OpenAI states it collects no transaction revenue initially, is not a bank or merchant for wallet purchases, and that agentic commerce remains early with some sites blocking agent purchases.
items.title: OpenAI Launches Payment Wallet for AI Agents in U.S.

items.summary: The urban thinktank Create Streets, with Cyclehoop, argues UK high streets should be revived through low-cost changes rather than multimillion-pound revamps. The report contends that replacing parking spaces with bike storage or outdoor dining generates more economic value: one 12-square-metre space holding nine e-bikes could yield around £146,000 annually in a market town, rising to over £300,000 in busier cities, versus just over £73,000 from parking. It also highlights outside dining adding roughly £120,000 yearly and cites Altrincham's retail vacancies falling from 30% to 7%. Andy Burnham announced a £210m regeneration fund in September, though most funding targets buildings rather than streets.
items.title: Thinktank Proposes Cheap High-Street Revamps Over Multimillion-Pound Projects

items.summary: Jaguar Land Rover reported a £451m quarterly loss in the July–September period, driven by costs from cutting 4,000 jobs amid tough trading conditions. Revenues rose to £5.9bn for the quarter. Chief executive PB Balaji urged the UK and EU to delay post-Brexit trade barriers as Chinese competition intensifies, while falling sales in China and the Middle East weighed on results.
items.title: Jaguar Land Rover Posts £451m Quarterly Loss After Job Cuts and China Competition Concerns

items.summary: The Indicator's newsletter examines whether European reliance on American air-defense technology has backfired, citing Bruegel's view that ignored calls to 'Europeanise' funding left a visible strategic gap. A Patriot missile backlog and production delays have locked buyers into unreliable supply while Russia remains the primary threat. The piece frames Trump as merely forcing an older warning about over-dependence, urging Europe to diversify away from U.S. systems.
items.title: Does Europe Regret Its Bet on U.S. Defense?

items.summary: A Microsoft Outlook outage beginning around 1pm ET Thursday disrupted email, calendar, video conferencing and cloud storage across the US. Local governments in Colorado, Maryland, Texas, Virginia and New York reported unavailable services—bond payments, water bill processing and school communications—while congressional staffers cited interference with legislative work. Schools urged flexibility; Microsoft attributed issues to connectors rather than cyber activity, noting intermittent recovery on Friday.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Disrupts US Companies, Schools and Local Governments

items.summary: Two candidates are vying to succeed Christine Lagarde at the European Central Bank, an EU official stated on Friday. The contenders are Pablo Hernández de Cos and former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot. France leans towards Hernández de Cos while Germany favors Isabel Schnabel for market operations.
items.title: France and Germany near deal on De Cos for ECB top job as EU confirms two candidates

items.summary: Jensen Huang departed Nvidia after 33 years, succeeded by longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO. Cognitive scientist Gary Marcus described how Nvidia effectively became 'a bank,' circularly financing AI firms that then buy its chips—OpenAI, Anthropic and CoreWeave among them—even amid profit struggles. Kress's cautious background may alter this approach while she faces potential federal and congressional investigations into China dealings.
items.title: Nvidia's Interim CEO Inherits Risky AI Bets and a Legal Mess

items.summary: A Microsoft outage disrupted services including the collaboration tool Teams, email client Outlook and AI software Copilot. The company attributed the problem to higher-than-usual stress on its servers while systems showed early signs of stabilisation as a fix was worked on. BBC technology reporter Shiona McCallum explained what is known about the incident.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Teams and Outlook

items.summary: A global Microsoft services failure since Thursday disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and email across Portugal's public sector. The Ministry of Health, the Government and numerous schools lost access to institutional tools, forcing ministers and teachers to rely on WhatsApp, Signal and an unaffected internal network. Despite progress reported by Microsoft through Friday afternoon, recovery remained incomplete as the company attributed the outage to a configuration update that overloaded servers.
items.title: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Portuguese government and schools

items.summary: October existing home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010, reaching 3.75m units down 8.8% year-over-year as mortgage rates rose toward three-year highs near 7.18%. The National Association of Realtors attributed the decline to elevated borrowing costs and inflation amid an Iran war, with sales weakening in the Midwest, South and West while Northeast activity held steady.
items.title: US Existing Home Sales Hit a 16-Year Low in October Amid Soaring Mortgage Rates

items.summary: A record number of wildfires burned more than 14,062 square miles this year in the U.S. While ash and organic matter from burned watersheds wash into streams feeding water treatment plants, utilities must shut off intakes to prevent contamination. New studies indicate these effects can persist for up to 15 years, raising concerns as climate change increases wildfire frequency and size.
items.title: Wildfires Threaten US Water Supplies for Years

items.summary: In CGTN's "Beyond the Horizon" series, Wilfredo Ramos of United Parcel Service (UPS) argues that opportunity in Asia-Pacific now depends on connectivity beyond physical infrastructure. He notes UPS has operated its own flights into China for 25 years, and trade flows have changed dramatically since then. True connectivity requires moving goods, information and documentation together through smarter digital systems and border processes. Rather than fewer controls, the goal is making borders more predictable via interoperable customs and clearer duties visibility. Ramos stresses resilience over pure efficiency: businesses increasingly seek multiple routes and markets to reduce dependence on any single source of demand. He warns that smaller firms often lack resources to manage trade complexity, so connectivity must become accessible opportunity for all.
items.title: An Asia-Pacific built for opportunity

items.summary: European leaders have resisted US President Donald Trump's proposal to revise the continent's security framework, which he floated with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev after suggesting a broad deal could involve all of Europe. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas argued existing institutions like NATO and the European Union already provide stability, while historian Michael Kimmage dismissed 'European security architecture' as Russian propaganda designed to frame the war favorably for Moscow. The article traces how Russia has long alleged US and NATO violations of 1990s non-expansion pledges, culminating in its invasions of Georgia (2008), Crimea (2014) and Ukraine (2022). Experts warn that any Russian-driven restructuring would undermine international law and leave Ukraine vulnerable. On Friday, European leaders rejected the demands outright; Germany proposed hosting a 'Coalition of the Willing' to fund Ukrainian defense.
items.title: The Dangers of Revising Europe's Security Architecture

items.summary: Kosovo's Prime Minister Albin Kurti says his country has completed its democratic and anti-corruption homework but still lacks EU candidate status four years after applying, because the European Council is not seeking a Commission opinion. Blaming internal EU dynamics rather than the five non-recognisers—Spain, Cyprus, Romania, Greece and Slovakia—he cites incremental progress such as Spain recognising Kosovo's passport and visa liberalisation, while accepting EU critiques of judicial reform.
items.title: Kosovo PM Kurti on EU candidate status bid

items.summary: Roberta Lipson, Chair Emeritus of the American Chamber of Commerce in China and founder of United Family Healthcare, argues that healthcare cooperation extends beyond improving medical services. Having lived and worked in China for nearly half a century, she views collaboration as a means to bring people closer and foster mutual understanding between two major Asia-Pacific economies facing how partnership can bridge differences and build trust.
items.title: Building China-US Trust Through Healthcare Cooperation

items.summary: EU leaders convened an AI summit in Dublin amid Russia's war on Ukraine, which cast a shadow over the gathering. Guest speaker Fabrice Pothier of Rasmussen Global highlighted Europe's limited computing capacity—barely 5% of global availability—and urged governments to strengthen Ukraine with more air defense interceptors rather than debate their own relevance.
items.title: Dublin AI Summit Overshadowed by Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: An ecology instructor at Merrimack College in Massachusetts argues that outdoor field courses are irreplaceable, offering students memorable experiences—such as handling a garter snake or encountering wildlife abroad—and fostering both an appreciation of nature and a conservation ethic. Drawing on the Baba Dioum idea that we conserve only what we love and understand, he notes how unpredictable fieldwork inspires wonder and critical thinking about complex natural systems. Colleagues reinforce this: Professor Larry Kelts's Global Field Studies Program sent students to sites including the Brazilian Amazon, Great Barrier Reef, Serengeti Plain, Galapagos Islands, Belizean reefs, and Jamaica; Kristy McDowell leads a Costa Rica course comparing U.S. and Costa Rican environmental policy; Jim Hanken emphasizes safety regulations and notes that field trips can be costly for lower-income students; John Morrissey recounts how a Jamaican reef ecology trip changed his career path.
items.title: Why Field-Based Ecology Labs Matter for Student Learning and Conservation Ethics

items.summary: Highway 1 (the Ring Road) links Afghanistan's major cities but became a crime and violence hotspot after September 11, 2001, especially between Kabul and Kandahar. Travelers faced extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. Correspondents Claire Billet and Sandra Calligaro revisited the road to assess its condition five years into Taliban rule.
items.title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'

items.summary: Russell Brand faces fresh allegations after six new accusers went public on Friday, per a report by The Times. One claims non-consensual sex; another alleges he continued intercourse after she asked him to stop. Several met him at stand-up shows the court said he used to pursue women. Brand has not responded. He was jailed for ten years in London over rape and sexual assault charges.
items.title: Six More Women Accuse Russell Brand of Sexual Offences

items.summary: Alice Huang, linked to ride-hailing firm Nanjing Lingxing Technology and investors Alibaba and Tencent, is at the center of a growing mystery. Her company Megaspeed reportedly grew from zero revenue to nearly $300 million within 12 months in 2024, with asset value surging from $32 million to almost $3 billion over two years while trading more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips—despite empty offices and Huang no longer officially registered as a director.
items.title: Mystery Behind Nvidia's Chips & Empty Offices

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage on November 13, 2026 halted corporate inboxes across India. Most companies routed work to Microsoft Teams while Outlook and Copilot failed; a Chennai financial GCC moved all internal correspondence there. Banking operations stayed unaffected, with HDFC Bank posting about its inbox taking the day off and Axis sharing an old-school face-to-face video. Zoho, Freshworks, Kissflow and Google Workspace users reported normal days, but several MSME workplaces faced real disruption.
items.title: How India Inc Navigated the Friday the 13th Microsoft Outage

items.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles posted a ₹5,451 crore consolidated loss for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2FY27), down from a ₹76,248 crore profit in Q2FY26 due to Jaguar Land Rover restructuring costs. Revenue rose 34 per cent to ₹96,340 crore, while record quarterly sales of 200,000 units reflected strong demand and EV growth of 90 per cent YoY.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Posts Q2 Loss Amid JLR Restructuring Charges and Record EV Sales

items.summary: Microsoft reported progress restoring its flagship software after an outage that paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses worldwide. The company attributed the disruption to a core process on some servers becoming overwhelmed, with no evidence of malicious activity or established technical cause. Users in more than 70 countries faced problems across Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 products, which serve over 450 million commercial users globally.
items.title: Microsoft's Prolonged Global Outage Highlights Tech Concentration Risks

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage, dubbed 'Microsoft 364' by users joking a day was lost, flooded social media with memes—Ed Helms celebrating, the This Is Fine dog, Clippy's revenge, and Avengers: Doomsday references. While many found relief from emails, others faced deadlines; brands like Encyclopaedia Britannica, Burger King, and Air India joined in.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Sparks Memes Amid Real-World Disruption

items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, enabling its always-on 'dots' agents to pay for purchases without exposing users' card details. Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, the service requires a security check such as Face ID or fingerprint scan on every transaction. It is initially available in the US to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards.
items.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI Agent Payments

items.summary: Microsoft's multi-hour global outage on Friday degraded Outlook, Teams, OneDrive and Office web services; the cited cause was servers failing automated health checks, shifting load to other machines that then destabilized. While not attributed to AI code, it arrives amid Microsoft's aggressive deployment—CEO Satya Nadella said up to 30% of its code is now AI-written—and a shift toward autonomous agents like GitHub Copilot CLI over Anthropic's Claude Code. Experts warn this reflects 'comprehension debt': as AI commits millions of lines faster than humans can review, no single engineer fully understands the system when failures occur. The outage also follows Microsoft letting go around 8,000 employees and rolling out a voluntary exit for more than 60,000 by December 9.
items.title: A Microsoft Outage and the Growing Cost of AI-Driven Code

items.summary: After co-founding and running Nvidia for three decades, CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid scandal on Thursday. For years CFO Colette Kress served as a counterweight to his aggressive risk-taking, clashing with him over financing deals—including an OpenAI Ohio project pared from $250 billion to $120 billion—that critics called a circular AI economy. Now the 59-year-old finance chief is interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor. Shares slumped 14% before closing down 4.3%. Some question whether Kress can preserve Nvidia's risk appetite; others note she may temper its confrontational stance on export controls.
items.title: Nvidia Names Colette Kress Interim CEO After Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Scandal

items.summary: Tata Motors reported a net loss of Rs 5,531 crore in Q2FY27 as revenue jumped 34% year-on-year to Rs 96,920 crore. Domestic passenger vehicle (PV) business hit an all-time quarterly high of Rs 20,400 crore (+51%), with volumes up 40%, driven largely by EVs surging 90%. However, margins slipped on adverse commodity and foreign-exchange pressures; EBITDA margin fell to 4% and profit before tax was at breakeven. JLR posted £5.9 billion revenue (+20.3%) but cut full-year guidance to an adjusted EBIT margin of 2-3% amid geopolitical risks, citing a planned £15-18 billion investment programme.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Q2 Results: Company reports net loss of Rs 5,531 crore; revenue jumps 34% YoY

items.summary: More than 16 hours after a global outage began around 11:30 pm IST on November 12, Microsoft reported incremental recovery but declined to call the service fixed. Charles Lamanna said availability and email delivery were improving across growing portions of affected infrastructure, with progress spreading from Asia Pacific through North America and Europe. The incident kept Outlook, Teams, Exchange Online, SharePoint, Copilot, Defender XDR, and consumer apps down; it originated in the Americas when servers unexpectedly went offline and could not handle load, rather than a traffic surge or cyberattack. Recovery remains variable, with intermittent access issues possible until full restoration—still without a timeline.
items.title: Microsoft's Microsoft 365 Outage Recovery Progresses Slowly Over More Than 16 Hours

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage beginning late Thursday, November 12 and continuing into Friday disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint Online and OneDrive. While Microsoft attributed the disruption to infrastructure problems—servers failing automated health checks, reduced capacity and an overwhelmed core process—the event sparked online conspiracy theories linking it to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure, a possible Chinese cyberattack on US communications infrastructure, and a rogue AI agent. Microsoft stated there is no indication of malicious activity or that China was responsible.
items.title: Conspiracy Theories Surrounding Microsoft Outage Amid Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary: India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a one-year high of $39.88 billion in October as imports rose sharply, driven by elevated energy prices amid the West Asia conflict and strong gold buying ahead of Diwali. Merchandise exports hit a record $49.47 billion (up 45% year-on-year), but petroleum imports alone jumped to $22.82 billion while total merchandise imports reached $89.35 billion, offsetting export gains.
items.title: India's October Trade Deficit Hits One-Year High on Surging Imports Despite Record Exports

items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs defended India's visa decisions as sovereign functions after allegations that over 100 foreign speakers invited to the two-day, ~1,000-delegate Bharat Summit in Hyderabad (Nov 13-14) were denied entry or had visas cancelled. Congress leaders blamed Home Ministry orders; Telangana CM Revanth Reddy and MP Shashi Tharoor attacked PM Modi, while former foreign secretary Kanwal Sibal criticized Norway.
items.title: India's MEA Defends Visa Denials at Congress Bharat Summit Amid Political Backlash

items.summary: NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri warned that India is not yet fully secure in meeting its food needs, importing more than half of its edible oil requirements. He noted surprising sources like Australian chana and Canadian masoor dal, plus imports from Myanmar, Africa and Russia. With 17 million metric tonnes worth about $20 billion imported annually, Lahiri cautioned that supply disruptions could become a strategic disaster.
items.title: NITI Aayog flags India's food import dependence on edible oils and pulses
